newsitem.title: UK: UK's ASDA to offer round-the-clock shopping.
newsitem.headline: UK's ASDA to offer round-the-clock shopping.

text.p: British supermarket company ASDA Group Plc on Thursday said it planned to test opening 24 hours a day, kicking off on election day to provide sustenance to voters fed up with a diet of non-stop politics.
The chain, known for its cheeky and innovative image, said it would start round-the-clock shopping at its Minworth, central England, store on May 1, and promises plenty to amuse jaded voters.
"There'll be pizzas, pies and hot punch for the punters and we'll be making sure we are stocked up with our Election Ales," a company spokesman said.
ASDA is selling three types of beer during the election, one representing each of the three major parties.

"Major's Mild," "Tony's Tipple" and "Ashdown's Ale" poke gentle fun at the policies of John Major's ruling Conservative party, Tony Blair's Labour party which currently heads the opinion polls and Paddy Ashdown's Liberal Democrats.
For those shoppers who still hunger for the polls, the store will be transmitting election results through the night on May 1, the spokesman added.
ASDA said the 24-hour opening at Minworth would run every day except Sundays, when opening times are limited by law to six hours a day.
The pilot, which could run for up to a year, would be monitored to assess customer reaction, a spokesman said.

It will mean non-stop shopping for over 131 hours a week. Although round-the-clock shopping is common in the U.S., in Britain -- where Sunday opening only started relatively recently -- it is limited to smaller groceries or corner shops in city centres, while in continental Europe shops generally close in early evening.
ASDA's in-house bakery will be cooking through the night while insomniacs can linger over a coffee at the in-house cafe, the company said.
The all-night opening will be staffed with volunteers and the project has created 35 new jobs, ASDA said.
